## Overview

Offline embedding refresh jobs are **scheduled batch processes** that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus when operational conditions change. Unlike on-demand embedding, they run on a fixed cadence and re-embed either the full document set or an incremental subset, then atomically swap new vectors into the retrieval index to prevent serving mixed-model results during the transition.

## When to Refresh

Embedding refreshes are triggered by:

- **Model change**: The underlying embedding model itself is upgraded or swapped
- **Bulk document updates**: Source documents change significantly and need re-embedding to maintain vector fidelity
- **Scheduled maintenance**: Periodic re-indexing on a fixed cadence

## Key Operational Characteristics

### Batch Processing
- Runs on a fixed schedule rather than on-demand
- Re-embeds the full corpus or an incremental subset
- Decouples embedding computation from query-time serving

### Atomic Index Swaps
- New vectors are staged independently before deployment
- The swap to production is atomic, avoiding any period where the index serves a mix of old and new embeddings
- Prevents quality regression by keeping results consistent during the transition

## Critical Operational Concerns

### Model Versioning
Every embedding batch must be tagged with the model version used. This enables:
- Tracking which documents were embedded with which model
- Correlation analysis if quality issues emerge post-deployment
- Clear audit trail for compliance or debugging

### Vector Drift Monitoring
Comparing old and new vector representations for the same documents reveals:
- Whether the new model produces substantially different embeddings
- Potential quality regression before going live
- Whether incremental updates skew the corpus semantically over time

### Blue-Green Staging
- Stage the new index (green) while the current index (blue) remains live
- Run validation queries against green before swapping traffic
- If quality regression is detected, roll back by keeping blue live
- Enables rapid recovery without re-running the embedding job

## Related Patterns

- [[blue-green-deployment]] — General strategy for atomic index or service replacement with rollback capability
- Vector search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems depend on embedding refresh reliability
